name: colAnyNAs
title: Checks if there are any missing values in an object or not

origin.description: Returns whether any selected element in a column is missing. This is the name to prefer over colAnyMissings. Implemented as colAnys(x, value = NA).
origin.usage: colAnyNAs(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, a list, a matrix, a data.frame, or NULL. These row and column forms take a matrix or a vector with dim.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.
Passed to rowAnys or colAnys. na.rm and dim. can be supplied here.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: Please use base::anyNA() instead of anyMissing(), colAnyNAs() instead of colAnyMissings(), and rowAnyNAs() instead of rowAnyMissings(). The row and column forms call rowAnys or colAnys with value NA and return as soon as a missing value is found in that margin.
origin.value: A logical vector. TRUE if a missing value was detected in that row or column, otherwise FALSE. NA is not produced by a search for missing values.
origin.example:
x <- matrix(c(TRUE, NA, FALSE, TRUE, NA, FALSE), nrow = 3)
colAnyNAs(x)

translation.description: Returns whether any selected element in a column is missing. This is the name to prefer over colAnyMissings. This calls colAnys with value=None.
translation.usage: colAnyNAs(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array, or a 1-d vector when dim is set. Double missing values are nan. Integer missing values are None or -2147483648. Logical missing values are None.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: Passed through to rowAnys or colAnys. Searching for a missing value does not drop missing values, so this does not change the result.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers, dim. in R. A 1-d x is filled column-major.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for useNames. The result has no names attached.

translation.details: colAnyNAs calls colAnys with value None, which is R's NA. The scan is the rowcounts or colcounts crate with what 1, counting missing values. It stops a margin at the first missing value.
translation.value: An object array of True and False, one per selected row or column.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowalls import rowAlls, colAlls, allValue, rowAnys, colAnys, anyValue, rowAnyMissings, colAnyMissings, rowAnyNAs, colAnyNAs

x = np.array([True, None, False, True, None, False], dtype=object).reshape((3, 2), order="F")
colAnyNAs(x)
